review.reviewBody: I used to spend hours every week ordering food. Now it's simple, super easy, and I have free time to spend on other aspects of my restaurant.

@graph.name: Three steps, and the first is a P21 export
@graph.description: Setup runs on one spreadsheet from P21 and installs nothing in it. Any EDI or API setup comes later, if you want it, and we go over what it would take on your side in the demo.

step.name: Export a report of each account's regular items
step.text: A P21 report saved as a spreadsheet is usually all we need. It lists each account's items and what that account pays.

step.name: We build each kitchen's guide
step.text: We set up each guide, the kitchen downloads the app, and most place a first order the same day.

step.name: App orders arrive at your desk
step.text: Each one comes checked by the kitchen, numbered and timed, in whichever format you set up.

@graph.name: Do we need a Prophet 21 alternative to cut down on phone orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Orders over the phone are a desk problem, not an ERP problem: P21 makes an order quick to enter once someone has it. Begin with the kitchens on the phone most often, and those orders no longer wait for someone to pick up the phone. P21 goes on running the counter, prices, inventory and accounting.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Prophet 21?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, at one job: a kitchen sending its order without tying up anyone at your desk. For everything after that, P21 is the system to keep, which is why this is an addition and not a Prophet 21 alternative.

@graph.name: Doesn't Epicor Commerce already let kitchens reorder online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Epicor Commerce, a separate web store product for P21, shows each account its own prices, with fast repeat orders and a quick order pad, open day and night. It still means signing in, searching and typing. We built ours for kitchens that find talking quicker than typing, and they check what they said before it goes.

@graph.name: We're planning the cloud move. Should we wait?

acceptedAnswer.text: No need. Nothing of ours is installed in P21, and setup works from a spreadsheet you export, so the move can happen before or after. If you later send orders by EDI or the API, check that part against your cloud plans in the demo.

@graph.name: Does our Prophet 21 link up with your app?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There is no ready-made link between them, and Epicor and we each support only our own software. Sent over EDI or the API, the order can pass into P21 with nobody retyping it, if your setup accepts it in that form; a demo will tell you whether it does. If it is emailed, the attached file has every line checked by the kitchen, and someone on your team keys it into P21 from that rather than from a call.

@graph.name: What about Epicor's own AI for Prophet 21?

acceptedAnswer.text: Epicor's AI, called Prism, helps people inside P21 get answers and find data, and an Epicor partner sells a product that reads emailed orders for your team. Both start once the order has reached you. None of the Prism agents Epicor lists for P21 lets a kitchen speak its order to you. Other vendors sell tools that help your reps enter P21 orders by speaking, or that turn customer texts into orders. Ours is the app a chef talks the order into.

@graph.name: How long does setup take, and is there a published price?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors, setup takes 24 to 48 hours, since we never need a P21 login and put no software on your servers. Epicor lists no price for P21 and we do not publish one either; you get ours as a quote.

What we say about other ordering tools comes from a search for ordering tools sold for P21, the same day. Epicor does not publish a P21 price, so none appears here.
